audit_findings.title: Probable fatal-accident liability is largely unaccrued and may exceed insurance coverage
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; as of 2026-06-30, $1.5 million of legal costs had been recognized, $0.9 million paid, $0.6 million accrued, and no damages liability recorded
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured damages or self-insured amount is a senior claim that reduces the equity bridge; related recurring premium increases could also reduce future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has concluded that a loss is probable in the case, but given the preliminary nature of the proceedings, the Company cannot reasonably estimate a range of possible losses at this time in excess of the amount accrued for legal costs.
audit_findings.explanation: A probable loss is disclosed, so this is more than a generic litigation risk, but the filing provides neither asserted damages nor applicable aggregate coverage. The five fatalities make a material equity claim plausible, while the available record cannot establish its amount or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the complaint and asserted damages, current case reserve, self-insured retention, complete primary and excess insurance tower, remaining aggregate limits, erosion from other claims, and insurer coverage positions; then deduct the probability-weighted uninsured exposure and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: TEL earnings and the $4.9 million stake bridge may describe different economic claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 TEL equity income was $14.709 million, distributions were $6.615 million, and the investment carrying value increased from $85.512 million at 2025-12-31 to $94.506 million at 2026-06-30, versus a $4.9 million bridge addition; the latest carrying-value gap is $89.606 million, or $3.24 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: TEL can enter through recurring OE, as a separately valued non-operating stake in the equity bridge, or both. Using both double-counts value; excluding TEL earnings while adding only historical invested cash can substantially understate value.
audit_findings.evidence: We have accounted for our investment in TEL using the equity method of accounting and thus our financial results include our proportionate share of TEL's net income, which amounted to $ 14.7 million in 2025 , $ 14.7 million in 2024 , and $ 21.4 million in 2023 .
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter inconsistency: the bridge uses the original $4.9 million contribution even though the filed economic claim has a much larger carrying value, while TEL equity income may already be embedded in OE. TEL supplied $14.709 million, or 82.2% of the $17.9 million anchor, so inconsistent treatment is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion. Carrying value is a scale reference, not proof of realizable value.
audit_findings.action: Trace TEL equity income, distributions, and related adjustments through every OE year. Either exclude TEL from OE and add a defensible realizable stake value, or include CVLG's share of TEL owner earnings after TEL maintenance capital and financing needs and remove the separate stake bridge amount; rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earnouts are debt-like claims omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.000 million at 2026-06-30, equal to $0.33 per diluted share and 3.1%-4.5% of the stated $198-$288 million scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Unfunded earnout principal reduces the equity bridge unless its settlement cash flows are already included in forecast OE; fair-value remeasurements should be normalized in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The contingent consideration liability is included in accounts payable and other long-term liabilities in our condensed consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing reduces the relevant liability from $22.489 million at year-end to $9.000 million after $13.146 million of payments. Even assuming the entire remaining liability was omitted and must be deducted immediately, the maximum direct reduction is $0.33 per share, insufficient to alter the stated valuation conclusion relative to $7.16-$10.42 scenario values and the $35.05 market price.
audit_findings.action: Verify the $9.000 million payment schedule and whether settlement cash flows are included in OE. Normalize contingent-consideration remeasurements and deduct any portion not captured in OE when refreshing the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may include a nonrecurring discontinued-operations recovery
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.829 million after tax, equal to 15.8% of the $17.9 million anchor; if retained dollar-for-dollar, approximately $30.0 million, $37.6 million, and $44.4 million of bear, base, and bull value, respectively, or $1.08, $1.36, and $1.60 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time discontinued-operations recovery included in the latest-year OE anchor is compounded through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating income for the years ended December 31, 2025 , of $ 3.8 million relates to the reimbursement to us from Triumph Bancorp, Inc. ("Triumph") for a portion of the $ 37.3 million of indemnification payments we made pursuant to the TFS Settlement between 2020 and 2023 (the "Indemnification Reimbursement").
audit_findings.explanation: The $2.829 million recovery is filed and demonstrably nonrecurring, but the supplied record does not show whether it was removed from OE. Its potential effect is large enough to change the scenario values materially, particularly because terminal value represents roughly half of operating PV.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2025 OE reconciliation and remove the entire TFS reimbursement and associated discontinued-operation tax effects if present; then recompute the anchor, forecast OE, terminal value, scenario values, and buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: A retained goodwill impairment could materially depress the latest-year anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.698 million pretax, equal to 59.8% of the $17.9 million anchor before any tax effect; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the noncash impairment reduces the latest-year OE anchor and is capitalized through forecast OE and terminal value despite creating no future cash claim.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of these factors, during the three months ended December 31, 2025, we performed an interim quantitative goodwill impairment test which resulted in a partial impairment of goodwill of $10.7 million within the Dedicated reportable segment for the legacy Dedicated reporting unit.
audit_findings.explanation: The impairment is a demonstrated one-time noncash charge, but the supplied valuation lacks an OE reconciliation showing whether it was added back. Its size relative to the anchor makes the possible understatement material. The exact value effect cannot be established without the applicable tax treatment and reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the $10.698 million goodwill impairment was added back with the correct tax treatment. Separately verify that recurring maintenance capital, fleet-disposal losses, and held-for-sale equipment economics were not removed with it; rerun all scenarios if the impairment remains in OE.
